claims.note: normalize: re.sub(r'\s+',' ', text.translate(QUOTE_FOLD)).strip(); docstring says it folds curly quotes (QUOTE_FOLD at L45 maps curly to straight). Nuance: leading/trailing whitespace runs are stripped rather than collapsed to one space, so a strict reader could call 'every run' inaccurate.
L20 CHOICE_SURE = 0.8 (auto-accept at >= 0.8), not 0.7; line is inside the section.
check_claim catches FileNotFoundError from read_text and returns verdict file_missing, review True (L333-336).
split_passages docstring: 'Paragraphs are never merged'; code only splits long paragraphs into PASSAGE_CHARS slices.
run_path = runs_dir / run_id[:7] / f'{run_id}.json'; docstring 'runs/<YYYY-MM>/<id>.json — month derived from the id's date prefix'; id format %Y-%m-%d_%H%M.
subprocess.run([claude_cmd, '-p'], input=prompt, ...) sends the prompt on stdin; docstring says 'the prompt goes via stdin'.
No matches returns 'No relevant past runs found for this task.', not ''.
Cache.get takes the lock only for lookup and insert; compute() runs outside it (L168-177).
memgate_verdict checks conflict (L272) before duplicate (L274); both high -> 'conflict'. Comment: 'A conflict outranks everything else'.
review = confidence < CHOICE_SURE; at exactly CHOICE_SURE review is False.
suggestion_block uses confidence >= GATE, so confidence == GATE emits the handler suggestion, not 'No handler stands out'.

Three stable sorts: app, then timestamp desc, then score desc -> final order is score, then recency, then app (verified by running the sort). Section shows the sort code; file docstring L48 also says 'score, then recency, then app name'.
_next_id starts n=1 and increments before building the suffix, so the first collision gets _2; docstring says '_2, _3, ...'.
Empty string is not None, so it skips the default branch; ''.strip().lower() is in _FALSEY -> returns False regardless of default (only coincides with default when default=False).
doc_freq == total gives log(1)+1 = 1; docstring: 'a token in every task still keeps weight 1.0'.
verdict = 'absent' if exists < FIND_ABSENT else 'partial'; exists == FIND_ABSENT -> 'partial'. Constant values not needed for the conditional claim.
skip if any(p <= lo for p in wanted); reuse == lo -> skip before the in_band check; conflict/duplicate checks come first. UNSURE_BAND value not needed.
Blank lines (normalize(line) == '') are skipped before ' '.join(parts); confirmed: locate_quote('a\n\nb', 'a b') -> (1, 3).
found = ['fast-worker', 'self'] -> len(set(found)) == 2 -> None.
store.proposed_path.unlink() runs unconditionally after the 'if new:' block, so it is deleted even when all bullets are duplicates.
' OFF '.strip().lower() == 'off' which is in _FALSEY -> False; _FALSEY is inside the section.
data['runs'] on a dict without 'runs' raises KeyError, which is caught -> rebuild_index().

Section shows read_text raising JevError when SECRET_NAME matches, but SECRET_NAME's pattern (L41-44) is outside the section. In the file, 'id_(rsa|dsa|ecdsa|ed25519).*' matches 'id_ed25519.pub' (confirmed), so it is refused.

Section shows scores['noise'] >= hi with lo, hi = UNSURE_BAND, but UNSURE_BAND = (0.3, 0.7) is at L19 (outside the section). File: hi = 0.7 and >=, so noise >= 0.7 -> skip after conflict/duplicate checks.
Section uses CLAIM_CONTEXT_LINES without its value; the file sets CLAIM_CONTEXT_LINES = 15 (L38), so it is 15 lines on each side, not 10.
route_passage uses > SCREEN['evidence_min']; the value 0.55 (L28) is outside the section. In the file 0.55 > 0.55 is False -> exclude/no_evidence, never include.
Section uses INDEX_FIELDS without its definition; the file's L14 INDEX_FIELDS = ('id', 'timestamp', 'task', 'outcome'), so there are no learnings.
Section shows v >= NOUL_YES but not its value; the file sets NOUL_YES = 0.5 (L35), so e.g. 0.45 is not 'yes'.
